**Note on citations:** The document is an HTML rendering with no page numbers, so I can't give page numbers. I cite section and equation numbers instead.

## The DPO loss (Eq. 7, Section 4)

$$
\mathcal{L}_{\text{DPO}}(\pi_\theta;\pi_{\text{ref}}) = -\mathbb{E}_{(x,y_w,y_l)\sim\mathcal{D}}\left[\log\sigma\left(\beta\log\frac{\pi_\theta(y_w\mid x)}{\pi_{\text{ref}}(y_w\mid x)} - \beta\log\frac{\pi_\theta(y_l\mid x)}{\pi_{\text{ref}}(y_l\mid x)}\right)\right]
$$

The terms are:
- **y_w and y_l** are the preferred and dispreferred completions for prompt x (Section 3).
- **σ** is the logistic function (Section 3).
- **β** controls how far the policy can deviate from the reference policy π_ref, which is usually the SFT model (Section 3, after Eq. 3).

The paper says this objective is "analogous to the reward modeling approach (i.e. Eq. 2)" (Section 4). That reward-model loss is −E[log σ(r_φ(x,y_w) − r_φ(x,y_l))] (Eq. 2, Section 3).

## What plays the role of the reward

The reward is the scaled log-ratio between the policy and the reference model. The paper defines the implicit reward as:

$$
\hat{r}_\theta(x,y) = \beta\log\frac{\pi_\theta(y\mid x)}{\pi_{\text{ref}}(y\mid x)}
$$

It calls this "the reward implicitly defined by the language model π_θ and reference model π_ref" (Section 4, "What does the DPO update do?").

This comes from the following derivation:
- **Eq. 5 (Section 4):** The optimal policy for the KL-constrained objective is rearranged to give r(x,y) = β log(π_r(y|x)/π_ref(y|x)) + β log Z(x).
- **Section 4, leading to Eq. 6:** The Bradley-Terry model depends only on reward differences, so the β log Z(x) term cancels. Only the log-ratio term remains.
- **Theorem 1 (Section 5.1; proof in Appendix A.6):** Under mild assumptions, every reward equivalence class consistent with the Plackett-Luce and Bradley-Terry models can be represented as r(x,y) = β log(π(y|x)/π_ref(y|x)). The reparameterization therefore loses no generality.
- **Section 4, introduction:** The paper concludes that "the policy network represents both the language model and the (implicit) reward."

The reference code in Appendix B computes the same quantity as `rewards = beta * (pi_logps - ref_logps).detach()`.
